games.name: Retro Snake
games.summary: Steer a growing snake around the field, eat apples and never bite your own tail.
games.description: The keypad classic, rebuilt from scratch. Every apple makes the snake longer and a little faster, and every fifth apple spawns a fading gold star worth a big bonus. Choose Classic (deadly walls), Wrap (walls wrap around) or Maze (inner walls) on the title screen. Turns are buffered so quick double-taps are never lost.
games.objective: Eat as many apples as possible without hitting yourself (or a wall in Classic and Maze modes).

games.name: Pixel Paddle
games.summary: Vertical table tennis against a CPU opponent that predicts your shots. First to 7 wins.
games.description: A portrait-friendly take on paddle tennis built for tall handset screens. Where the ball meets your paddle sets the return angle, every rally speeds the ball up, and the CPU predicts wall bounces with a deliberate margin of error that shrinks on harder settings.
games.objective: Score 7 points before the CPU does by getting the ball past its paddle at the top of the table.

games.name: Block Fall
games.summary: Rotate and drop falling four-block pieces to clear rows, in endless Marathon or a 40-line Sprint.
games.description: A falling-blocks puzzle tuned for a phone keypad: delayed auto-shift on 4 and 6, rotation in both directions, a ghost piece showing where the block lands, hard drop on 0 or #, and a fair shuffled bag so you never wait forever for a long piece. Marathon speeds up every ten lines; Sprint 40 is a race against the clock.
games.objective: Clear rows by filling them completely. Marathon: survive and score. Sprint 40: clear 40 lines in the shortest time.

games.name: Mine Sweep
games.summary: Deduce where the mines are from the numbers and open every safe square.
games.description: The logic classic for a keypad: move with 2/4/6/8 (or diagonally with 1/3/7/9), open with 5 and flag with 0 or #. The first square is always safe, opened numbers can be chorded, and boards larger than the screen scroll with the cursor so even the 16x16 field works on a 128x128 display.
games.objective: Open every square that does not contain a mine, as fast as you can.

games.name: Keypad Chess
games.summary: Full-rules chess against an alpha-beta AI with three strengths, played entirely on the keypad.
games.description: Complete chess rules - castling, en passant, promotion, check, checkmate, stalemate, the 50-move rule and insufficient material - with an integer-only alpha-beta search tuned for handset CPUs. Easy looks one move ahead with some randomness, Normal searches two plies plus captures, Hard searches three plies plus captures. Legal moves are highlighted, and your win/loss/draw record is saved on the phone.
games.objective: Checkmate the computer's king.

games.name: Brick Buster
games.summary: Bounce the ball off your paddle to smash eight hand-built walls of bricks, with power-up capsules.
games.description: A brick breaker with eight original layouts, multi-hit and steel bricks, and four capsule power-ups (wide paddle, multi-ball, slow ball and extra life). The return angle depends on where the ball meets the paddle, and the second time through the levels the ball is faster.
games.objective: Clear every breakable brick on each level without losing all three balls.

games.name: Number Place
games.summary: Fill the 9x9 grid so every row, column and box holds 1-9. Fresh puzzles generated on the phone, always with exactly one solution.
games.description: A number-placement logic puzzle with an on-device generator: a valid grid is shuffled, then clues are removed one at a time while a bitmask backtracking solver proves the solution stays unique. Two input styles cover every handset: Keypad mode (2/4/6/8 move, 5 opens a number picker) for phones without a joystick, and Direct mode (# toggles) where digits write straight into the cell. Clashes are highlighted and matching digits glow.
games.objective: Complete the grid correctly in the shortest time.

games.name: Pixel Jumper
games.summary: Run, jump and stomp through eight scrolling levels of pits, spikes, springs and walking blobs.
games.description: A side-scrolling platformer with variable-height jumps, coyote time and jump buffering so the keypad feels responsive. Levels come from a seeded generator that only builds gaps and ledges within jumping range, so all eight stages are the same every time you play and always beatable. Collect 100 coins for an extra life.
games.objective: Reach the flag at the end of all eight levels.

games.name: Traffic Dash
games.summary: Weave through highway traffic at speed, grab fuel cans and chain near-misses for a bigger score.
games.description: A lane-switching highway racer. Traffic drives slower than you, some cars signal and change lanes, fuel drains constantly and is topped up by green cans, and brushing past cars builds a near-miss combo. The spawner always leaves at least one lane open, so every crash is avoidable. Rush Hour mode doubles the traffic.
games.objective: Drive as far as you can without running out of fuel or crashing three times.

games.name: Tower Guard
games.summary: Build and upgrade Arrow, Cannon and Frost towers along the road to hold back 20 waves of monsters.
games.description: A compact tower defence designed around a cursor and the 5 key. Three tower types each have three upgrade levels, monsters come in normal, fast and armoured varieties, every fifth wave ends with a boss, and you can call waves early with # for bonus gold. Three maps: Meadow, Canyon and the long Spiral.
games.objective: Survive all 20 waves without losing your 20 lives.

games.name: Star Defender
games.summary: Defend the planet from a marching alien formation, hiding behind shields that crumble under fire.
games.description: A fixed-shooter with an original cast of pixel aliens. The formation marches faster as it shrinks and drops lower each time it hits a wall, shields erode block by block from both sides, a mystery ship drifts across the top now and then, and every new wave starts a little closer to the ground.
games.objective: Destroy every alien in each wave before the formation reaches the ground. Three lives.

games.name: Tile Merge
games.summary: Slide numbered tiles around the board and merge equal pairs until you build the target tile.
games.description: The sliding number puzzle where equal tiles combine into their sum. Tiles glide smoothly, merged tiles pulse, and one undo per move rescues a slip of the thumb. Three boards: the classic 4x4 race to 2048, a tight 3x3 to 256 and a roomy 5x5 to 4096.
games.objective: Create a tile with the target number (2048 on 4x4) before the board fills up.

games.name: Four Drop
games.summary: Drop discs into a seven-column grid and line up four before your opponent - against the CPU or a friend.
games.description: The vertical four-in-a-row game built for the keypad: press 1-7 to drop straight into a column, or steer with the joystick. The CPU uses alpha-beta search with a window-scoring evaluation at depth 2, 4 or 6, and a hot-seat mode lets two people share one phone. The starting player alternates every game and your record against the CPU is saved.
games.objective: Connect four of your discs in a row - horizontally, vertically or diagonally.

games.name: Twenty-One
games.summary: Play the dealer at the classic 21 card game: hit, stand or double, and grow 100 chips into 1000.
games.description: A clean table game of twenty-one dealt from a four-deck shoe. Hit, stand or double down with the keypad, the dealer draws to 17, and a natural 21 pays 3 to 2. Start with 100 chips; reach 1000 to beat the house, or go broke trying. Your best peak bankroll is saved. Splitting and insurance are not included to keep the game simple on small screens.
games.objective: Grow your bankroll from 100 to 1000 chips.

games.name: Dungeon Quest
games.summary: A pocket roguelike: explore ten generated dungeon floors, level up, and slay the dragon at the bottom.
games.description: Every floor is a fresh set of rooms and corridors revealed by line-of-sight field of view. Movement is turn-based, so take your time: bump into monsters to fight them, gather potions, gold, weapons and armour, and level up as you descend past rats, goblins, skeletons, orcs, trolls and wraiths. Press # for a map of everything you have explored.
games.objective: Reach floor 10 and defeat the dragon.

games.name: Spot Kick
games.summary: A football penalty shoot-out where the goal is mapped onto your keypad: press 1-9 to place your shot or pick your dive.
games.description: Five kicks each, then sudden death. When shooting, choose one of nine target zones with the matching number key and stop the power meter in the green - blast it and it may sail over the bar, scuff it and the keeper reaches it easily. When saving, watch the run-up and press a number to dive. Keepers get sharper at Pro and Legend level.
games.objective: Score more penalties than the CPU in the shoot-out.

games.name: Pocket Farm
games.summary: Till, plant, water and harvest a 30-plot field and earn $1000 before the 28-day season ends.
games.description: A bite-sized farming sim driven by one context key: 5 tills, plants, waters or harvests depending on the plot. Four crops with different growth times and prices, daily market swings, an energy budget that forces you to sleep, rain forecasts that save you a watering run, and crops that wither if left dry for three days. Play the 28-day Season challenge or farm forever in Endless mode.
games.objective: Earn $1000 within the 28-day season.

games.name: Echo Tones
games.summary: A light-and-sound memory game played on the keypad itself: repeat ever-longer sequences of tones.
games.description: The screen mirrors the phone's 3x3 number pad, so every light corresponds to a real key under your thumb. Each round the phone plays one more note, faster than before; repeat it exactly. Classic mode uses the four cross keys, Keypad mode all nine, and Reverse mode makes you play the tune backwards. Fully playable without sound thanks to the lights.
games.objective: Repeat the longest sequence you can.

games.name: Rock Blaster
games.summary: Pilot a drifting vector ship through wrap-around space, splitting tumbling rocks and dodging a sharpshooting saucer.
games.description: Inertia-based space shooting drawn entirely with lines. Rotate with 4/6, thrust with 2 and fire with 5 while rocks split from large to medium to small. A saucer cruises through and aims at you, hyperspace is an emergency escape that might land you somewhere worse, and every 10000 points earns an extra ship. All physics use fixed-point integer maths for old handsets.
games.objective: Clear wave after wave of rocks and survive as long as possible.

games.name: Crate Pusher
games.summary: Push crates onto targets in 20 original warehouse puzzles, each verified solvable with a known minimum push count.
games.description: A box-pushing logic puzzle with 20 original levels produced by a reverse-play generator and checked by a breadth-first solver, which also supplies the par (fewest possible pushes) shown for every level. Unlimited undo, instant restart, saved progress and free choice of any unlocked level from the title screen.
games.objective: Push every crate onto a target square. Try to match the par push count.

games.name: Noughts Grid
games.summary: Noughts and crosses where the keypad is the board - plus a 5x5 four-in-a-row variant.
games.description: On the classic board, keys 1-9 map one-to-one onto the squares, so playing feels like pressing the grid itself. The Perfect CPU uses full minimax and never loses; Easy makes human mistakes. The 5x5 board needs four in a row and has a heuristic CPU, and both boards support two players on one phone.
games.objective: Get three (or four on 5x5) of your marks in a row.

games.name: Sky Hopper
games.summary: An endless vertical jumper: bounce from platform to platform, steering left and right, and climb as high as you can.
games.description: Your hopper bounces on its own; you only steer. Platforms are spawned within jumping range, then mix in sliding, crumbling, one-use cloud and spring platforms as you climb. The sky darkens into a starfield the higher you go, screen edges wrap around, and stars on platforms give bonus points.
games.objective: Climb as high as possible without falling off the bottom of the screen.

games.name: Moto Rush
games.summary: A pseudo-3D motorbike race down a winding, rolling highway against the clock.
games.description: Classic sprite-scaler racing rendered with nothing but triangles and integer maths: a 600-segment road with eased curves and hills, alternating rumble strips, roadside trees and posts, and slower traffic to weave through. Curves push you outward, grass slows you down, collisions send you sliding, and each checkpoint adds time. Two tracks: the gentle Coast road and the steep, twisty Mountain pass.
games.objective: Ride as far as possible, reaching each checkpoint before the timer hits zero.

games.name: Sea Strike
games.summary: Hunt the enemy's hidden fleet on an 8x8 sea before their admiral finds yours.
games.description: A hidden-fleet naval duel. Shuffle your fleet until you like the layout, then trade shots with a CPU admiral. Cadet fires at random, Captain hunts around every hit, and Admiral also sweeps the sea in a checkerboard and follows ship lines. Fewer shots means a higher score.
games.objective: Sink all five enemy ships before your own fleet is destroyed.

games.name: Klondike
games.summary: The classic patience game: build four suits from Ace to King, with Draw 1 and Draw 3 rules.
games.description: Full Klondike solitaire designed for a joystick or the 2/4/6/8 keys. A single cursor walks the stock, waste, foundations and seven columns; pressing 2 inside a column grows the selection to pick up a whole run. Press # to fling a card to its foundation, and once every card is face-up the game finishes itself automatically. Long columns compress to fit even a 128-pixel screen.
games.objective: Move all 52 cards onto the four foundations.

controls.action: Change row / grow or shrink run selection

games.name: Monster Duel
games.summary: Raise a monster partner and battle through eight trainers with turn-based, element-driven combat.
games.description: Pick Emberpup, Ripplefin or Thornbud and take on a gauntlet of eight trainers ending with the Champion. Six original species and six elements interact through a strengths-and-weaknesses chart, speed decides who strikes first, Guard halves incoming damage, and at level 8 your partner learns a devastating special move with limited uses. Experience, levelling and potions carry you through.
games.objective: Defeat all eight trainers, including the Champion.

games.name: Mini Golf
games.summary: Nine top-down crazy-golf holes with bank shots, bumpers, sand traps and water hazards.
games.description: Aim with 4/6 (fine-tune with 1/3), stop the swinging power meter with 5 and watch the ball carom around the course. Walls bounce, bumpers kick the ball back harder, sand drags it to a crawl and water costs a penalty stroke. Hit the cup too hard and the ball skips straight over it. Par 29 for the nine holes; your best round is saved.
games.objective: Complete all nine holes in as few strokes as possible.

games.name: Lake Fishing
games.summary: Cast from the dock, strike at the bite and play the fish on a tension meter. Six species, one golden rarity.
games.description: A relaxed one-button fishing sim. Cast distance decides depth, and depth decides what bites: minnows in the shallows, bass and pike further out, catfish in the deep and a very rare golden carp anywhere. Strike too early and you spook the fish; reel too hard and the line snaps; let it go slack and the fish throws the hook. The sky turns to sunset over a four-minute day, and your record catch is saved.
games.objective: Score as many points as possible in a four-minute day (or ten casts).

games.name: Multitap Rush
games.summary: Type falling words with old-school multi-tap texting (press 2 three times for C) before they hit the ground.
games.description: A typing game that only makes sense on a phone keypad. Words rain down and you spell them with the letters printed on the number keys. Smart mode accepts each letter the instant you reach it on the key, so it is a pure speed test; Classic mode is authentic multi-tap where you pause or switch keys to confirm, and mistakes break your combo. Longer words unlock as you go.
games.objective: Type as many words as possible before three of them reach the ground.

games.name: Fruit Catcher
games.summary: Slide your basket to catch falling fruit, chain combos and dodge the bombs.
games.description: A quick-fire catch game with pixel-art fruit. Apples, bananas, grapes and melons are worth more the rarer they are, golden stars are worth 100, and catching in a row builds a multiplier. Magnets widen the basket, clocks slow time, and bombs cost one of your three hearts. Drop ten pieces of fruit and it's over. The pace rises every 20 seconds.
games.objective: Score as many points as possible without catching three bombs or dropping ten fruits.

games.name: Slide Fifteen
games.summary: The sliding tile puzzle: put the numbers back in order by sliding tiles into the gap.
games.description: The pocket puzzle that predates phones, in three sizes: the quick 3x3 Eight, the classic 4x4 Fifteen and the brain-melting 5x5 Twenty-four. Shuffles are generated from legal moves, so every board is solvable. Tiles slide smoothly, rows are colour-coded and tiles already in their home square glow. Your lowest move count for each size is saved.
games.objective: Restore the tiles to numerical order in as few moves as possible.

games.name: Flip Disc
games.summary: Outflank and flip your opponent's discs on an 8x8 board - against a positional CPU or a friend.
games.description: The classic disc-flipping strategy game. Legal moves are dotted, flips animate, the last move is marked and passes are announced automatically. The CPU combines a positional weight table (corners good, squares next to corners bad) with mobility in an alpha-beta search one, two or three plies deep. Your best disc count against the CPU is saved.
games.objective: Have more discs of your colour than your opponent when neither side can move.

games.name: Cave Escape
games.summary: Explore six flip-screen caverns, climb ladders, collect five crystals and find the key to escape.
games.description: A compact flip-screen exploration platformer in the style of 8-bit cave games. Walk off a screen edge to reach the next cavern, climb ladders between levels, dodge swooping bats and floor spikes, and gather the five crystals. An iron door guards the exit and only opens for the key. Your fastest escape time is saved.
games.objective: Collect all five crystals and the key, open the door and reach the exit as fast as you can.

games.name: Checkpoint Rally
games.summary: A top-down rally time trial: steer a free-rotating car through numbered checkpoints over two laps.
games.description: Rally driving viewed from above on a scrolling 40x40 stage. The car rotates smoothly through 256 headings with speed-sensitive steering; dirt road is fast, grass and water slow you down and trees stop you dead. An on-screen arrow always points to the next checkpoint. Two stages - Forest and Lakeside - each with a saved best time.
games.objective: Pass every checkpoint in order and complete two laps in the fastest time.

games.name: Box Claim
games.summary: Dots and boxes: draw lines, complete boxes to claim them, and avoid handing your opponent a chain.
games.description: The pencil-and-paper classic on a 4x4 or 5x5 board. The cursor glides between the lines of the grid, completed boxes are stamped with their owner and the last line drawn is highlighted. The standard CPU grabs free boxes and avoids giving away third sides; the Smart CPU also simulates how many boxes each forced move would hand you and picks the cheapest. Two players can share the phone too.
games.objective: Claim more boxes than your opponent.

games.name: Hi-Lo Cards
games.summary: Guess higher or lower to climb a seven-card ladder, doubling the prize each rung - bank it or risk it all.
games.description: A push-your-luck card game in ten rounds. Each correct higher-or-lower call doubles the prize, from 10 up to 1000 at the top of the ladder; a single wrong call loses it. Live odds computed from the cards remaining in the deck help you decide when to bank, and one card swap per round can rescue you from a dreaded middle card.
games.objective: Bank as many points as possible over ten rounds.

controls.action: Swap the current card (once per round)

games.name: Island Dig
games.summary: Comb a random island with a metal detector and three compass readings to dig up three buried chests.
games.description: A turn-based treasure hunt on a freshly generated island. Each step drains energy and updates your metal detector, which beeps louder as you close in on an unfound chest. Three compass readings point the way when you are lost. Digging turns up coins, coconuts and junk as well as treasure, while wandering crabs pinch anyone who gets in their way.
games.objective: Dig up all three treasure chests before your energy runs out.

games.name: Ten Pin
games.summary: Ten frames of bowling with pin-to-pin collisions and proper strike and spare scoring.
games.description: Choose your release point, stop the swinging aim arrow and time the power meter, then watch the ball crash into the rack. Pins are simulated as circles that pass momentum to each other, so a ball into the pocket really does scatter the deck. Full ten-frame scoring with strike and spare bonuses and a three-ball tenth frame; a perfect game is 300.
games.objective: Score as many points as possible over ten frames (maximum 300).

games.name: Corner Shop
games.summary: Stock the shelves, set your prices and read the weather to turn $50 into a fortune in 30 days.
games.description: A pocket shop-keeping sim. Each morning check the forecast, buy six kinds of stock at wholesale and set selling prices; then open the doors and watch customers walk in. Hot days sell ice cream, rain sells umbrellas, overpricing drives people away, empty shelves cost reputation, and bread, milk and ice cream spoil if left on the shelf. A daily report shows sales, costs and spoilage.
games.objective: Finish 30 days with as much cash as possible ($200 counts as a win, $500 is excellent).

games.name: Mole Bonk
games.summary: Nine molehills laid out like your keypad: press 1-9 to bonk moles, but never the bunnies.
games.description: A reflex game that turns the phone's number pad into the playing field - each hole sits exactly where its key is under your thumb. Moles rise and duck back down faster as time goes on, golden moles pay five times as much, bunnies cost you points and your combo, and a run of hits multiplies your score. Play a 60-second Classic round or Endless, where three escapes end the game.
games.objective: Score as many points as possible by bonking moles (Classic: in 60 seconds; Endless: until three escape).

games.name: Gem Swap
games.summary: Swap neighbouring gems to line up three or more, setting off cascading chain reactions.
games.description: A match-three puzzle with six differently shaped gems, so colours stay readable even on washed-out screens. Gems animate as they swap and fall, cascades multiply your score, invalid swaps bounce back, a hint glows if you hesitate and the board reshuffles itself when no moves remain. Play 30 Moves for strategy or 90 Seconds for speed.
games.objective: Score as many points as possible within 30 moves or 90 seconds.

games.name: Keypad Checkers
games.summary: English draughts with forced captures, multi-jumps and kings, against a three-level CPU.
games.description: Full rules of English checkers: men move diagonally forward, captures are mandatory, multi-jump sequences must be completed and men reaching the far row are crowned. The CPU runs an alpha-beta search that follows jump chains to the end, two, four or six plies deep. Legal destinations are marked, the last move is highlighted and the status line reminds you when a capture is forced. Your record is saved.
games.objective: Capture or block all of the CPU's pieces.

games.name: Ladder Loot
games.summary: Grab every gold bar on a screen of ladders, ropes and bricks while guards chase you - dig holes to trap them.
games.description: A single-screen action puzzle platformer. Run, climb ladders and hang from ropes to collect the gold; dig through the brick floor beside you with 1 and 3 to trap pursuing guards, but get clear before the hole fills back in. Taking the last bar raises an escape ladder to the next level. Levels come from a generator that always joins every floor with a ladder, and more guards join as you progress.
games.objective: Collect all the gold on each level and escape up the ladder that appears.

games.name: Drag Strip
games.summary: Quarter-mile drag races won on launch revs and perfectly timed gear shifts, with a garage full of upgrades.
games.description: A timing-based racer built around a tachometer. Rev the engine during the countdown to nail the launch, then shift up through five gears when the needle hits the green band - too early bogs the engine, too late bounces off the limiter. Beat five rivals of rising skill, and spend your prize money on engine, gearbox and tyre upgrades between races.
games.objective: Beat all five rivals to become drag strip champion.

games.name: Land Grab
games.summary: Pick a colour to flood your territory into matching neighbours - out-grow the CPU to own the board.
games.description: A two-player territory game on an 11x11 board of six colours. You expand from the bottom-left, the CPU from the top-right; each turn you choose a colour (never your own or your opponent's) and absorb every touching tile of it. Press 1-6 to pick instantly. The clever CPU weighs not only its own gain but also which colours would most help you next turn.
games.objective: Own more than half of the board.

games.name: Draw Poker
games.summary: Jacks-or-better video poker: hold cards with keys 1-5, draw once, and get paid by the table.
games.description: Classic five-card draw video poker. Bet one to five credits, hold the cards you want with the number keys 1-5 (one key per card, left to right), and draw replacements once. A full pay table is always on screen and lights up the winning hand, from jacks or better up to a 4000-credit royal flush at maximum bet. Grow 100 credits into 1000 to break the bank.
games.objective: Grow your 100 starting credits to 1000 without going broke.

games.name: Lost Keep
games.summary: A graphical text adventure: explore a ruined keep, solve item puzzles and restore the tower's gem - no typing needed.
games.description: A classic illustrated adventure redesigned for a keypad. Every room is drawn on screen, and instead of typing commands you pick from a menu that only lists what makes sense right now: look, go somewhere, take what you see, or use what you carry. Ten rooms, seven items and a chain of puzzles involving a hungry hound, a locked library, a dark cellar and a ghostly knight. Fewer moves earns a better score.
games.objective: Find the stolen gem and return it to the statue at the top of the tower.

games.name: Hoop Shot
games.summary: A 60-second basketball shoot-out: time the aim and power, bank it off the glass, and catch fire.
games.description: Side-on basketball with real projectile physics. Stop the swinging aim arrow, then the power meter, and the ball arcs toward the hoop where it can rattle off the front or back of the rim, kiss the backboard or drop clean through. Shots from beyond the arc are worth three, the shooting spot moves after every basket, and three in a row sets you on fire for double points.
games.objective: Score as many points as possible in 60 seconds.

games.name: Deep Mine
games.summary: Drill deep for coal, gold and diamonds, sell your haul at the surface and upgrade your pod to reach the core.
games.description: A mining sim with a little pod and a lot of dirt. Drill sideways and down, fly back up on thrusters, and manage fuel, hull and cargo space as ore gets richer with depth: coal, iron, silver, gold, ruby and diamond. Sell at the surface shop, refuel, repair and upgrade your drill, fuel tank, cargo bay and hull. Undiggable rock, gas pockets, lava and long falls stand between you and the ancient core 600 metres down.
games.objective: Reach and drill into the ancient core at the bottom of the mine.

games.name: Orbit Jump
games.summary: A one-button space hop: break orbit at the right moment to be captured by the next planet up.
games.description: Your ship circles each planet automatically - your only control is when to let go. Launch along the tangent of your orbit, sail across the gap and get caught by the next planet's gravity field (shown as a faint ring). Stars beside each planet are worth bonus points, later planets spin faster and drift sideways, and missing everything costs one of three ships.
games.objective: Hop as far up the planet chain as you can.

games.name: Light Trails
games.summary: Light-cycle duels: leave walls of light behind you and be the last rider standing.
games.description: Arena survival against one or three AI riders. Every bike paints a permanent wall as it moves; the AI chooses turns by measuring how much open space each direction leaves it, so it fights for territory rather than driving randomly. Turns are buffered so quick taps register, and a rechargeable boost lets you cut opponents off. First to three round wins takes the match.
games.objective: Win three rounds by being the last light cycle still riding.

games.name: Pixel Logic
games.summary: Picture-logic puzzles: use the number clues on every row and column to reveal hidden pixel art.
games.description: Fourteen original picture-logic puzzles - six 5x5 warm-ups and eight 10x10 pictures. Clues list the runs of filled cells in each line; fill cells with 5 and mark known blanks with 0. Clues grey out as their line becomes correct, the cursor's row and column clues are highlighted, and any grid that satisfies every clue counts as solved, so you are never punished for an alternative solution. Progress is saved.
games.objective: Fill the grid so every row and column matches its clues.

games.name: Five Stones
games.summary: Five in a row on an 11x11 board, against a CPU that weighs every open three and four.
games.description: The ancient five-in-a-row stone game. Place black stones on the intersections and be first to an unbroken line of five. The CPU scores every candidate point for both attack and defence using open-ended run patterns, so it will block your open threes and pounce on your mistakes; Easy is more forgiving. A two-player mode lets friends share the phone. The winning line is drawn and the last stone is marked.
games.objective: Be the first to place five stones in an unbroken line.

games.name: Treasure Run
games.summary: An endless temple runner: jump pits and crates, slide under beams and scoop up gems as the pace builds.
games.description: Your explorer sprints automatically; you decide when to jump, double-jump and slide. Pits, crates and low stone beams come thicker and faster the further you get, gems arc over the obstacles to tempt risky jumps, and a rare shield orb absorbs one hit. Score is distance plus ten per gem.
games.objective: Run as far as you can without falling or crashing.

controls.action: Jump (again in the air to double jump)

games.name: Snow Slalom
games.summary: Carve down the mountain through 25 flag gates against the clock - or freeride through the forest.
games.description: A top-down downhill race. Your skis have five angles: pointing straight down is fastest, while wide carves scrub off speed but get you across the slope. Tuck for extra speed, snowplough to slow down, and thread every red and blue gate; each one you miss costs five seconds, and trees and rocks send you tumbling. Giant slalom has wide gates, Slalom tight ones, and Freeride is an endless forest run.
games.objective: Pass through every gate and reach the finish line in the fastest time (Freeride: ski as far as you can).

games.name: Kingdom Ledger
games.summary: Rule a small kingdom for ten years by deciding how much land to trade, grain to feed and acres to sow.
games.description: A resource-management classic in the spirit of the earliest computer strategy games, rebuilt for a keypad. Each year set three numbers - land to buy or sell, grain to feed your people and acres to sow - then read the royal report of harvests, rat raids, starvation, newcomers and the occasional plague. Starve too many in one year and you are overthrown; survive ten years and you are judged on land per person and lives lost.
games.objective: Survive ten years with a growing, well-fed population and plenty of land per person.

games.name: Cell Solitaire
games.summary: The all-cards-face-up patience game with four free cells - nearly every deal is winnable.
games.description: A free-cell style solitaire with full multi-card moves: the game works out how many cards you can move at once from your empty free cells and columns, so you never have to shuffle a run by hand. Safe cards fly to the foundations automatically, # sends any card home, and long columns squeeze to fit small screens. Your fastest solve is saved.
games.objective: Move all 52 cards to the four foundations, in suit from Ace to King.

controls.action: Change row / grow or shrink run

games.name: Pocket Saga
games.summary: A tiny console-style RPG: roam the overworld, fight random battles, shop in towns and defeat the Dark Knight.
games.description: A complete pocket role-playing adventure. Walk a scrolling overworld of plains, forests, rivers and mountains where monsters grow tougher the further you roam. Battles are turn-based with Attack, Magic (heal or fire), Potions and Run. Two towns offer an inn and a shop for potions and weapon and armour upgrades, a cave hides the Hero Sword behind three fights in a row, and the Dark Knight waits in the castle to the north-east.
games.objective: Grow strong enough to defeat the Dark Knight in his castle.

games.name: Pocket Cricket
games.summary: Chase down a target in a two-over, super-over or five-over run chase - pick the shot and nail the timing.
games.description: A batting game built around reading the delivery. Each ball has a line (leg, middle, off), a length (yorker, full, good, short) and a pace; play to the leg side with 4, the off side with 6, loft it straight with 2 or block with 8, timed to the moment the ball arrives. Perfect timing finds the boundary, short balls sit up to be hit, yorkers are hard to score from, lofted shots risk a catch and leaving a straight ball can cost your stumps.
games.objective: Score the target runs before you run out of balls or wickets.

games.name: Diner Rush
games.summary: Run a busy diner single-handed: the room is laid out like your keypad, so key 1-6 sends your waiter to that table.
games.description: A time-management restaurant game designed around the number pad. Tables sit where keys 1-6 are and the kitchen hatch where key 8 is, so serving becomes muscle memory. Take orders when guests raise a hand, drop them at the kitchen, carry up to two plates back, serve before patience bars run out, and clear tables for the next guests. Quick service earns bigger tips, every fifth meal in a row earns a streak bonus and three walk-outs end your shift.
games.objective: Earn as much money as possible in a three-minute shift without three guests walking out.

games.name: City Shield
games.summary: Aim a crosshair and launch interceptors to protect six cities from falling, splitting warheads.
games.description: Missile defence for the keypad. Glide the crosshair with the direction keys (or diagonally with 1/3/7/9) and press 5: the nearest of three bases with ammo fires an interceptor that bursts exactly where you aimed. Blasts chain through anything that flies into them, later waves bring splitting warheads and faster descents, and every wave pays a bonus for surviving cities and unspent ammo.
games.objective: Survive as many waves as possible without losing all six cities.

games.name: Switch Grid
games.summary: Every switch flips its neighbours too - turn all the lights off. On the 3x3 board, the keypad is the grid.
games.description: A light-switching logic puzzle in three flavours. Keypad 3x3 maps keys 1-9 straight onto the switches, Classic 5x5 uses a cursor, and Wrap 5x5 lets neighbours wrap around the edges. Each puzzle is built by pressing random switches, so it is always solvable; finish within par for a bonus. Twenty increasingly scrambled levels.
games.objective: Turn every light off, ideally within the par number of presses.

games.name: Seed Sowing
games.summary: A count-and-capture mancala-family game: sow seeds round the board, earn free turns and capture across.
games.description: One of the world's oldest kinds of board game, played with the classic store-and-capture rules. Press 1-6 to sow one of your pits and watch the seeds drop one at a time; landing in your store earns another turn and landing in an empty pit of your own captures the pit opposite. The CPU plans ahead with an alpha-beta search that understands free turns, or play a friend on one phone.
games.objective: Finish with more seeds in your store than your opponent.

games.name: Gravity Flip
games.summary: A one-button runner that cannot jump - flip gravity to fall between floor and ceiling past holes and spikes.
games.description: You sprint along an endless corridor where the only move is reversing gravity. Tap to fall to the ceiling, tap again to drop back to the floor, dodging holes and spike strips on both surfaces. The generator never blocks both surfaces at once, so every death is a timing mistake, and the pace never stops increasing.
games.objective: Run as far as possible without falling out of the corridor or hitting spikes.

games.name: Hill Climb
games.summary: Drive a little 4x4 over endless rolling hills - feather the gas, tilt in the air and land on your wheels.
games.description: A side-view physics driver over procedurally generated hills that grow steeper the further you go. Gravity pulls you back on climbs and launches you off crests; in the air, 4 and 6 tilt the car so you can land on your wheels (clean landings earn a bonus, landing on your roof ends the run). Fuel cans keep the tank topped up and coins add to your score.
games.objective: Drive as far as possible before you flip over or run out of fuel.

games.name: Galaxy Conquest
games.summary: Real-time space strategy: send fleets between planets to out-produce and overwhelm the red empire.
games.description: Planets of different sizes build ships at different rates. Jump the cursor between planets with the direction keys, pick a planet you own and a target, and half its ships launch. Fleets that land on enemy or neutral worlds battle the defenders and capture the planet if they outnumber them. The CPU picks targets by value and distance, and on Admiral it also reinforces its weak worlds. Every map is freshly generated.
games.objective: Capture every red planet and destroy every red fleet.

controls.action: Jump to the nearest planet in that direction

games.name: Eights Shed
games.summary: Shed your hand by matching suit or rank - eights are wild - against one to three CPU players.
games.description: The classic shedding card game. Match the top card's suit or rank, play an eight at any time to name a new suit, and draw when you're stuck. CPU opponents keep the suits they hold most, save their eights for emergencies and warn you when they're down to their last card. Winning scores the points left in the other players' hands (eights are worth 50).
games.objective: Be the first player to play every card in your hand.

games.name: Arena Champion
games.summary: Gladiator duels: read high and low wind-ups, block to stun, punish the opening, and upgrade between six bouts.
games.description: Timing-based arena combat. Each opponent telegraphs attacks high or low; block to match and they are stunned for a double-damage counter. Quick strikes are safe, heavy strikes hit three times harder and interrupt wind-ups but drain stamina. Later gladiators wind up faster and feint. After every win pick an upgrade: strength, armour, stamina or vitality.
games.objective: Defeat all six gladiators to become Arena Champion.

games.name: Court Rally
games.summary: Top-down tennis against the CPU: time your swing to aim, rally, and win a three-game set.
games.description: A compact tennis game seen from above. Slide along the baseline and press 5 as the ball arrives; swing early to pull the shot one way, late to push it the other, or press 2 for a lob. Balls are judged in or out on the first bounce, a second bounce loses the point, and full tennis scoring with deuce and advantage is used. Pro mode speeds up the ball and sharpens the CPU.
games.objective: Win three games before the CPU does.

games.name: Tiny City
games.summary: Zone homes, shops and factories, lay roads and power, and grow a town of 2000 citizens in ten years.
games.description: A pocket city builder on a 12x12 map with a winding river. Zones grow on their own when they touch a road and sit within reach of a power plant; residents need jobs, jobs need residents, parks help neighbourhoods and factories next to homes hold them back. Monthly taxes pay for road and power upkeep, bridges cost extra, and the goal is 2000 citizens within ten years. Sandbox mode has unlimited money.
games.objective: Reach a population of 2000 within ten years without going bankrupt.

games.name: Road Hopper
games.summary: Hop a frog across five lanes of traffic and a log-strewn river into the homes at the top.
games.description: The hopping-across-the-road arcade idea, built from scratch: dodge cars and trucks moving at different speeds, then ride drifting logs and turtles across the river without being carried off the screen. Each frog that reaches an empty home scores a time bonus; fill all five to clear the level and face faster, denser traffic.
games.objective: Fill all five homes on each level before your lives run out.

games.name: Pipe Flow
games.summary: Rotate pipe tiles to connect the water inlet to the drain - every grid is generated around a guaranteed solution.
games.description: A plumbing puzzle where each tile is a straight, bend, junction or cross. The generator lays a random self-avoiding route from inlet to drain, fills the rest with decoy pipes and spins every tile, so each board is solvable but never the same. Water spreads live through connected pipes as you rotate, so you can see your progress. Fifteen levels on a 5x5 or 7x7 grid; fewer turns score more.
games.objective: Connect the inlet on the left to the drain on the right on every level.

games.name: Nim Sticks
games.summary: The ancient take-away game: remove sticks from one row per turn - take the last (or avoid it in misere).
games.description: Rows of matchsticks, two players, one rule: take any number of sticks from a single row. Normal play rewards taking the final stick; misere play punishes it. The standard CPU blunders now and then, while the Expert CPU plays the mathematically perfect nim-sum strategy - you can still win, but only from a winning position and without a single slip. Boards are the classic 1-3-5-7 or randomly dealt.
games.objective: Normal: take the last stick. Misere: force the CPU to take it.

games.name: Barrel Climb
games.summary: Climb five girders by ladder while barrels roll down at you - jump them for points.
games.description: A single-screen climbing platformer. Barrels are thrown from the top, roll along each girder, drop off its open end and occasionally tumble straight down a ladder - including the one you're on. Walk, hop and climb your way to the top girder; every barrel you leap scores 100 and each stage the barrels roll faster and more often. Ladder positions change every stage.
games.objective: Reach the top girder on every stage without getting hit.

games.name: Pixel Racer
games.summary: Top-down three-lap circuit races against three AI drivers on two Grand Prix tracks.
games.description: Wheel-to-wheel racing from above. Start from a grid, slipstream your way through the pack, brake for the tight corners and keep off the grass. AI rivals follow the racing line and ease off for bends, cars bump and slow each other in close combat, and the HUD shows your live position. Oval GP is fast and flowing; Twisty GP tests your braking.
games.objective: Finish the three-lap race in first place.

games.name: Grid Tactics
games.summary: Turn-based squad battles on an 8x8 field: move, attack, use cover and outmanoeuvre the red army.
games.description: A pocket tactics game. Your four units - Soldiers, an Archer and a Knight - each move and attack once per turn; movement ranges are highlighted, archers shoot from three squares away, units in trees take reduced damage and rocks block the way. The enemy AI weighs every reachable square to focus down your weakest unit. Win three battles against growing armies on randomly generated fields.
games.objective: Defeat the enemy army in three consecutive battles.

games.name: Memory Cards
games.summary: Turn over cards two at a time and find all the matching pairs - solo or in a duel against a forgetful CPU.
games.description: The classic pairs memory game played with a deck of cards. Solo modes on a 4x4 or 5x6 layout reward finishing in the fewest turns. In Duel mode you and the CPU alternate, a match earns another go, and the CPU remembers only some of the cards it has seen - so it is beatable, but it will pounce on any pair it knows.
games.objective: Find every matching pair (solo: in the fewest turns; duel: more pairs than the CPU).

games.name: Deep Crawl 3D
games.summary: A first-person step-and-turn dungeon crawler: find three rune stones and the stairs on each of three maze floors.
games.description: Old-school first-person dungeon exploration rendered with nothing but filled triangles: corridors, side openings and dead ends recede into the gloom four squares deep. Each floor is a freshly carved maze with loops. Collect the three glowing rune stones to unlock the stairs, bump-fight the green slimes that block the corridors, and check the auto-map of everywhere you have seen with #.
games.objective: Collect three runes and take the stairs on each of three floors.

games.name: Bullseye
games.summary: Target archery: steer a swaying sight, hold your breath to steady it and allow for the wind.
games.description: Twelve arrows across three distances - 30, 50 and 70 metres. The sight drifts with your breathing and sways more at long range; hold 0 to steady it, but your breath runs out and the sway gets worse while you recover. A wind flag shows how far each arrow will drift, so aim off into the wind. Ten-ring scoring with every arrow hole left in the target face.
games.objective: Score as many points as possible with twelve arrows (maximum 120).

controls.action: Hold breath to steady the aim

games.name: Factory Line
games.summary: Run a sorting line: open the right chute with keys 1-3 as each coloured part rolls past.
games.description: A frantic factory sim. Red, green and blue parts (and grey scrap) ride a conveyor past three chutes leading to colour-coded bins. Keys 1, 2 and 3 toggle the chute gates; a part over an open gate drops straight in, and scrap must ride to the end of the belt. Correct sorts build a combo, wrong bins earn strikes, and the belt keeps getting faster.
games.objective: Sort as many parts as possible before making three mistakes.

games.name: Copter Cave
games.summary: Hold to climb, release to sink: fly a helicopter through an endless, narrowing cave.
games.description: The purest one-button arcade challenge. Your helicopter climbs while you hold the key and sinks when you let go; the cave meanders, slowly closes in and starts sprouting rock pillars as you fly deeper, while the scroll speed creeps up. Distance is your score and your best flight is saved.
games.objective: Fly as far as possible without touching the cave or the rock pillars.

games.name: Code Breaker
games.summary: Deduce a hidden code of coloured pegs from black and white feedback markers.
games.description: The classic code-cracking deduction game. Each colour sits on its own number key, so entering a guess is just a few taps; the cursor advances automatically and # submits. After every guess you see how many pegs are the right colour in the right place (black) and the right colour in the wrong place (white). Play the standard 4 pegs / 6 colours in 10 guesses, or the tougher 5 pegs / 8 colours in 12.
games.objective: Crack the hidden code in as few guesses as possible.

games.name: Race Home
games.summary: A cross-and-circle dice race: roll a six to leave base, race round the board and knock rivals back home.
games.description: The family dice race in pocket form. Each player has three tokens; a six brings one out of base and earns another roll, tokens race once round the 28-square track and then up their own home lane, and landing exactly on a rival sends it back to base - except on the starred safe squares. Play one or three CPU opponents who capture greedily, play safe when they can and always bring new tokens out on a six.
games.objective: Be first to get all three of your tokens home.

games.name: Wall Kick
games.summary: Wall-jump your way up an endless shaft, timing each kick to dodge spikes while the screen keeps rising.
games.description: A one-button vertical climber. You cling to a wall and slowly slide down it; press 5 to kick off and leap diagonally up to the opposite wall. Spike strips line both walls, gems sparkle in risky spots, and the camera climbs on its own - faster the higher you get - so hesitating is as deadly as jumping into spikes.
games.objective: Climb as high as possible without hitting spikes or falling behind the rising screen.

games.name: Ring Racer
games.summary: Fly a behind-the-ship space race through a course of rings - every ring adds time to the clock.
games.description: A pseudo-3D flying racer drawn with integer perspective: rings and mines rush towards you out of a starfield and you steer so each ring passes around your ship. Rings add two seconds and build a streak multiplier, mines knock five seconds off, boost trades control for speed, and the course spreads out and speeds up the further you get.
games.objective: Fly through as many rings as possible before the clock runs out.

games.name: Siege Lanes
games.summary: Three lanes, two castles: spend gold to send spearmen, archers and knights up a lane with keys 1-3.
games.description: A real-time lane battle for the keypad. Gold trickles in; pick a troop type and press 1, 2 or 3 to deploy it into the left, middle or right lane. Spearmen are cheap, archers strike from range and knights soak up damage. Troops fight anything they meet and batter the enemy castle if they break through, while the CPU reinforces whichever lane you are pushing hardest.
games.objective: Destroy the enemy castle before your own falls.

controls.action: Deploy to left / middle / right lane

games.name: Domino Line
games.summary: Draw dominoes against the CPU with a double-six set: match the open ends, draw when stuck, go out first.
games.description: A clean game of draw dominoes. The highest double opens, tiles must match one of the line's two open ends, and if you can't play you draw from the boneyard. Press 1 or 3 to choose which end, or 5 to let the game pick the end that fits; playable tiles light up in your hand. The CPU dumps its heaviest tiles first. Going out scores the pips left in your opponent's hand; a blocked game goes to the lighter hand.
games.objective: Play all your dominoes before the CPU does.

games.name: Spell Deck
games.summary: A pocket deck-building duel: draw four spells, spend three mana, read the foe's intent and grow your deck after each win.
games.description: Fight through five foes with a ten-card starter deck. Every turn you draw four spell cards and have three mana to spend on strikes, fireballs, wards, heals, life drains and freezing frost. Each enemy telegraphs its next move, so you know when to block and when to go all in. Beat a foe and pick one of three new cards to add to your deck before the next battle.
games.objective: Defeat all five foes, ending with the Lich King.

games.name: Puck Rush
games.summary: Fast table air hockey against a CPU opponent: slide your mallet, bank off the rails and score first to seven.
games.description: An arcade air-hockey table squeezed onto a phone screen. Drive your mallet around your half with the joystick or the 1/3/7/9 diagonals; a mallet in motion transfers its speed to the puck, so swing through your shots. The CPU chases loose pucks in its half and falls back to guard its goal. Casual and Pro modes change how fast the CPU reacts.
games.objective: Score seven goals before the CPU does.

games.name: Lemon Stand
games.summary: Run a lemonade stand for fourteen days: read the forecast, tune your recipe, price and batch size, and build a reputation.
games.description: A bite-sized business sim. Every morning brings a weather forecast; you choose how sweet to make the lemonade, what to charge and how many cups to prepare before opening. Hot days and heatwaves bring crowds, rain keeps them home, and the forecast is not always right. Balanced lemonade at a fair price grows your reputation and your future customer count, while unsold cups are poured away at the end of the day.
games.objective: Finish the fourteenth day with as much cash as possible.

games.name: Bubble Shot
games.summary: Aim, bank off the walls and pop groups of three matching bubbles before the ceiling pushes down.
games.description: A classic aim-and-fire bubble popper built for the keypad. Sweep the launcher with 4 and 6, fire with 5 and swap with the next bubble using 0. Match three or more of a colour to pop them, and cut loose any bubbles hanging below for a bigger bonus. Every few missed shots the ceiling pushes down a new row; let the cluster reach the dashed line and it is over. Relaxed mode uses four colours and a slower ceiling.
games.objective: Clear every bubble from the board.

games.name: Laser Mirrors
games.summary: Rotate mirrors to bounce a laser beam through every crystal; fifteen generated puzzles with walls, decoys and bolted mirrors.
games.description: A laser fires in from the left wall of a 7x7 board. Move the cursor onto a mirror and press 5 to flip it between its two diagonals, steering the beam until it passes through every target crystal. Later puzzles add stone blocks that stop the beam, decoy mirrors and mirrors bolted in place. Each puzzle is built from a real beam path, so a solution always exists; fewer rotations earn more points.
games.objective: Light every crystal in all fifteen puzzles.

games.name: Peg Jump
games.summary: Peg solitaire on three boards: jump pegs over each other until only one remains, with unlimited undo.
games.description: The old wooden-board puzzle in your pocket. Pick up a peg with 5, then press a direction to jump it over a neighbour into an empty hole, removing the peg you jumped. Play the classic 33-hole cross, a smaller diamond, or a 15-hole triangle where diagonal jumps along the slope are allowed. Press 0 to undo as far back as you like. Fewer pegs left is better; a single peg in the centre of the cross is the master finish.
games.objective: Leave as few pegs on the board as possible, ideally just one.

games.name: Volley Beach
games.summary: One-on-one beach volleyball: run, jump and head the ball over the net, with three touches a side.
games.description: A sunny side-on volleyball match between two round beach players. Run with 4 and 6 and jump with 2 or 5; where the ball strikes your head decides its angle, so get under it to pop it up and jump into it to drive it over the net. You get at most three touches before the ball must cross. The CPU reads the ball's flight and leaps for blocks, more often on Hard.
games.objective: Win the match by reaching seven points first.

games.name: Pet Pal
games.summary: Hatch an egg and raise a pixel pet to adulthood: feed it, play with it, clean up and tuck it in.
games.description: A pocket virtual pet that grows up in about four minutes. Watch an egg hatch, then keep four needs topped up - food, fun, cleanliness and rest - while your pet grows from baby to child, teen and adult. Neglect costs health, messes make it sick and medicine cures it, but overfeeding and needless medicine do harm. Playtime is a quick left-or-right guessing game. A well cared for pet becomes a special happy adult.
games.objective: Raise your pet to adulthood in good health.

games.name: Space Trader
games.summary: Buy low and sell high across six worlds in thirty days, dodging pirates and chasing price spikes to pay off your loan.
games.description: A compact space trading sim. Every planet produces some goods cheaply and pays a premium for others, prices drift each day, and news of shortages and gluts can double or halve a market. Fill your hold, plot a course on the star map, and watch your fuel: longer hops cost more days and more fuel, and fuel is cheaper on the outer moons. Pirates may raid your cargo on arrival. Expand your hold when you can afford it, and finish day thirty with as much money as possible after repaying the loan.
games.objective: End day 30 with the highest net worth after repaying your loan.

games.name: Rail Switcher
games.summary: The keypad is a signal box: flip seven sets of points with keys 1-7 to route coloured trains to matching stations.
games.description: An experiment in using the number pad as a control panel. A branching railway fans out from a single line into eight coloured stations, with seven sets of points along the way, and each point is mapped to one number key. Trains roll in from the left one after another; flip the points ahead of them so every train ends up at a station of its own colour. Trains speed up and arrive closer together as you deliver more, and three wrong deliveries end your shift.
games.objective: Deliver as many trains as possible before making three mistakes.

games.name: Morse Signal
games.summary: Turn the 5 key into a telegraph key: tap out words in Morse code or read a flashing signal lamp against the clock.
games.description: A playful Morse code trainer built around the phone keypad. In Send mode the 5 key becomes a telegraph key - a quick tap is a dot, a longer press is a dash, and a short pause ends the letter. Key whole words letter by letter while the code for each letter is shown, and build combos for clean sending. In Receive mode a lamp flashes and beeps a letter; pick the right one from four choices with keys 1-4, answering before the signal ends for a bonus. Each round lasts 90 seconds.
games.objective: Score as many points as possible in 90 seconds.

games.name: Math Blitz
games.summary: Rapid-fire mental arithmetic typed straight on the number pad, checked the instant you enter the last digit.
games.description: The number pad was made for this. Sums, differences, products and divisions appear one after another and you type the answer directly; there is no confirm key, because the answer is checked the moment you have typed enough digits. Sprint mode gives you 60 seconds, with every correct answer adding a second. Survival puts a shrinking timer on each question and gives you three lives. Streaks raise the difficulty and mistakes ease it back down.
games.objective: Solve as many problems as possible before time or lives run out.

games.name: Cell Garden
games.summary: Plant a handful of seeds and let them grow by cellular-automaton rules; score the plants that end up on golden soil.
games.description: A gardening puzzle built on a classic cellular automaton. Each generation, an empty plot with exactly three living neighbours sprouts, and a plant with two or three neighbours survives while the rest wither. In Challenge mode you get a limited number of seeds and a set number of generations; plan a pattern that blooms across the golden fertile plots and holds there when the growing stops. Five gardens per game. Sandbox mode gives unlimited seeds with run, pause and single-step controls for free experimenting.
games.objective: Have as many plants as possible on golden plots when the final generation ends.
